findings.summary: host_parity.canonical_inventory() hardcodes <root>/plugins/tdd-playbook and refuses a vacuous family, so it raises FileNotFoundError in EVERY vendored layout (Claude and Codex, both reproduced by scratch install). It had no production bin/ caller, so nothing had ever exercised that path; D3's reviewer binding would have been the first, taking review_ledger's DEFAULT validate verb dark on exactly the downstream hosts it serves.
findings.disposition: New blocking prerequisite D0: host_parity.agents_roster()/agents_dir() resolve source, Claude-vendored and Codex-vendored layouts and return None instead of raising, on the catalog_rows degradation contract. canonical_inventory is untouched — its vacuity refusal is correct for parity duty, and weakening it would have traded one correct invariant for another.

findings.summary: The plan's judgment-vs-mechanical partition for the participation report would have been a third copy of a classification the repo already derives — and test_agents.py's existing PINNED/INHERIT split already disagrees with its OWN docstring on mutation-runner, the exact member the partition needed to exclude.
findings.disposition: The partition was DELETED rather than sourced: participation_report prints the whole roster and flags nothing, so nothing can be false-flagged. The record-authoring marker is derived by reading the briefs, not listed. Separately D8 corrected the contradicting docstring — the PINNED set was right, the sentence was not.

findings.summary: The participation report's only named consumer was run_calibration, which is opt-in and triggered by 'a verifier misbehaves'. An adversary named in no record cannot misbehave, so the report would have been dark in precisely the condition it exists to surface — dark by construction, not by omission.
findings.disposition: Routed the block into render_reference.review_section(), regenerated at every release, in addition to the recurrence verb. The test asserts at the CONSUMER — it reads the committed docs/reference/current-state.md — so a producer that stops being read goes red rather than passing on its own output.

findings.summary: The plan claimed a single grandfather cutoff kept append-only records valid 'through any future agent rename'. It does not: a post-cutoff record naming architecture-adversary breaks if that file is renamed later. The cutoff only grandfathers records predating the rollout.
findings.disposition: Replaced with a stated TWO-part contract: the cutoff for the rollout, plus agent filenames as canonical ids — already frozen by test_agents.py:111 and :588, so this NAMES an existing constraint rather than adding one — with a renamed id joining NON_AGENT_REVIEWERS as a historical alias. No alias table, no versioned ids.

findings.summary: The plan's 'dated debt' section carried an owner and nothing else — no capability id, expiry, done condition, or validate --as-of proof. That is prose parking, and it violates this repo's own deferral contract.
findings.disposition: Both deferrals registered as integration_debt with owner, expiry and done condition (loop-closed-contracts-unparsed 2026-10-31; codex-skill-surface-absent 2026-11-15), each demonstrated to RED at expiry+1 via validate --as-of and to stay quiet today. A third item (the mutation-runner docstring) was cheap enough to promote out of debt and shipped as D8.

findings.summary: The plan's end-to-end verification installed only the Claude surface and asserted Codex behaviour in a comment — on a deliverable whose entire premise is cross-layout portability. It also called render_reference.py with no argument, which runs check, not render.
findings.disposition: D0's tests drive the PRODUCTION installer for both hosts in fresh temp trees, import the VENDORED copy rather than only the source module, and cover the empty-directory case. The verification block now runs render then check.

findings.summary: README and capabilities.json still described the calibration cadence v1.32.0 retired — 'on a schedule', 'weekly', and a 14-day staleness check that 'runs inside the blessed gate'. The README contradicted itself within a few lines, and check_staleness.py appears in neither gate-manifest.json, gate_runner.py, nor .github/workflows/gate.yml, so both surfaces claimed a mechanism that does not run.
findings.disposition: D7, promoted into Phase 1 because it is wrong today and independent of the deferred doctrine work. Both surfaces now state that calibration is opt-in, that check_staleness gates nothing and is invoked by nothing, and what the opt-in posture trades away.

findings.summary: External review asserted that 0 of 39 records carry a recurrence_key, and concluded the new key should be framed as a first-instance class rather than an existing taxonomy.
findings.rationale: Refuted by counting: 24 of 39 records carry at least one recurrence_key, and 90 of 178 findings are keyed. The reviewer confirmed the correction in the following round and attributed it to a path-resolution error on their side. The premise being false inverts the conclusion — the taxonomy is well established, so the operative rule is to REUSE an existing key, which this record does for five of its eight findings rather than minting new vocabulary.
